entities.summary: Prince Bolasodun Adesumbo "Bola" Ajibola, SAN, KBE, CFR was a Nigerian jurist, who was the Attorney General and Minister of Justice of Nigeria from 1985 to 1991 and a judge of the International Court of Justice from 1991 to 1994. He was president of the Nigerian Bar Association from 1984 to 1985. He was also one of five commissioners on the Eritrea-Ethiopia Boundary Commission, organized through the Permanent Court of Arbitration. In 1979, he founded The Nigeria Institute of Chartered Arbitrators (NICArb) as the premier arbitration institute in Nigeria and it was duly incorporated in 1988 under the Companies Act as a legal entity Limited by Guarantee.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Attorney General and Minister of Justice of Nigeria from 1985 to 1991, Bola Ajibola played a crucial role in shaping Nigeria's legal landscape. His appointment as a judge of the International Court of Justice from 1991 to 1994 further underscored his significance in regional and international law.
